content: A Bachelor of Science (commonly abbreviated as BSc, BS, or less frequently as SB or ScB, derived from the Latin term Scientiæ Baccalaureus) is an undergraduate academic degree awarded upon the successful completion of a program that typically spans three to five years, depending on the country and institution. In the United States, the Bachelor of Science degree is often more specialized than a Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree, with a greater emphasis on the core subject and less focus on a broad liberal arts curriculum. For instance, a BS in Economics may require more advanced coursework in economics and additional supporting subjects, such as statistics, compared to a BA in Economics. The BS degree is also commonly associated with professional fields of study, including engineering, journalism, accounting, and advertising. Notably, some institutions, such as the California Institute of Technology (Caltech) and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), as well as the four U.S. service academies (United States Military Academy, United States Naval Academy, United States Air Force Academy, and United States Coast Guard Academy), confer the BS degree for all disciplines, even in traditionally non-scientific fields like literature. In the United Kingdom and Canada, the classification of subjects as science varies between universities. For example, an economics degree may be awarded as a BA at one institution but as a BSc at another. Certain universities, such as the London School of Economics, offer the BSc designation for nearly all subject areas, even those typically associated with the arts. Conversely, institutions like Oxford and Cambridge (collectively referred to as Oxbridge) predominantly award arts degrees, a practice rooted in historical and traditional conventions. The designation for a Bachelor of Science degree is typically BSc or BS for a standard degree, and BSc (Hons) or BS (Hon) for an honors degree. In Germany, the BSc was historically equivalent to a BSc (Hons). However, many German-speaking countries have transitioned to the Bachelor/Master (Ba/Ma) system, which includes the full equivalent of a BSc. Historically, at the University of Oxford, the BSc was a postgraduate degree, but this has since been renamed to MSc, although the degree itself is still actively conferred. In Brazil, the Bachelor of Science degree is considered a graduation-level qualification and is more specialized. It typically includes a mandatory one-year probationary period at the end of the program, followed by comprehensive written and oral evaluations, often referred to as a Monografia. Typical Completion Periods by Country Three Years In many countries, the Bachelor of Science degree is completed in three years. These countries include Australia, Austria, Barbados, Belgium, Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, the Slovak Republic, the Czech Republic, Denmark, England (three or four years if a one-year industrial placement is included), Estonia, Finland, France, Germany (usually three years, though some programs may extend to four), Hong Kong, Hungary, Iceland, India, Italy, Jamaica, Latvia, Malaysia, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Northern Ireland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Quebec, Scotland (non-Honors degrees), Singapore, South Africa, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Trinidad and Tobago, Wales, and Zimbabwe. Four Years In other countries, the Bachelor of Science degree typically requires four years of study. These include Afghanistan, Albania, Bangladesh (three or four years depending on the program), Bahrain, Brunei, Bulgaria, Canada (except Quebec), Croatia (four or five years), Guatemala, Greece, Indonesia, Iran, Iraq, Ireland, Israel, Japan, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Korea, Malta, Mexico, Myanmar, Pakistan, the People's Republic of China, the Philippines, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Scotland (Honors degrees), Slovenia, Taiwan, Turkey, Sri Lanka, Haiti (three or four years), the United States, and Zambia (four or five years).
